summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Shinichi Tsuda studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his Ph.D. at the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham. He held posts at Toyo Bunko, Eastern Institute, and ICPBS.

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University from 1984 to 1992. He held an academic post at Tottori University (1993–1999) and served as a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2009.

Shinjo Hinonishi was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He served at Koyasan University, where he was an assistant professor (attested 1980) and later a professor (attested 2008).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Kawasaki studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others. He served as a lecturer at the University at Buffalo (~1968–1970) and was a professor at the University of Tsukuba (1975–1997).

Shinjo Suguro was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, served as vice director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra in 1980, and was a professor at Rissho University (~1965–1996).

Shinjosei Mochizuki specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) and the University of Tokyo, and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University around 1966.

Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University (graduating in 1951) and Taisho University, later serving as a professor emeritus at Waseda University.

Murakami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University under scholars including Ensho Kanakura. He served as a professor at Tohoku University (~1977–1996) and also held a post at Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Nakai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966) and served as president and professor emeritus at Bukkyo University (~2005–2009).

Shinkō Mochizuki studied at Bukkyo University, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928), held multiple administrative and professorial posts at Taisho University (~1926–1942), and was a Japan Academy member in 1947.
Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi, Charles Hallisey (doctoral supervisor), and Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Nagoya University in 1995 and was attested as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1934–1959) and served as a professor at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kazunobu Matsuda, served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005), and worked as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna under Eli Franco, later teaching at Shinshu University (~2008–2018).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, Matsumoto studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020) and was a visiting professor at the University of Chicago in 2001.

Shiv Nath Sharma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947), and served as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Shiv Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (2018–2024) and held a postdoctoral researcher post at the Indian Council of Social Science Research in 2026.
